case_name: Robert O. Edwards, Jr. v. Douglas A. Collins
court: United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims

issues.label: Board jurisdiction under AMA lane
issues.why: The court must confirm the Board acted within the evidentiary limits of the direct review docket under 38 U.S.C. §§ 7113(a) and 7105.

issues.label: Record-closure date correctness
issues.why: The court must determine the correct evidentiary record cutoff (the AOJ decision on appeal, March 26, 2020) and what materials are legally within it.

issues.label: Constructive possession doctrine scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether NAS Update 2012 (and/or Update 2010) was constructively before VA at the time of the AOJ decision and therefore part of the record.

issues.label: Constructive possession prerequisites
issues.why: The court must apply the requirements for constructive possession (e.g., relevance and reasonable connection to the claim/VA’s control) to NAS reports.

issues.label: AMA effect on constructive possession
issues.why: The court must address how constructive possession operates in the AMA framework with closed records and whether it can add materials not physically in the claims file.

issues.label: Board error re Update 2012 as argument
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board erred by treating Update 2012’s contents as impermissible even as legal/medical argument rather than new evidence.

issues.label: Judicial notice possibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether NAS reports are subject to judicial notice or otherwise usable without violating AMA evidentiary limits.

issues.label: Duty to assist timing
issues.why: The court must determine whether any duty-to-assist error occurred at the AOJ stage (where it matters for AMA remands) rather than at the Board stage.

issues.label: Duty to assist—medical exam standard
issues.why: The court must apply 38 U.S.C. § 5103A(d) (McLendon-type elements) to decide if VA had to provide an exam/opinion.

issues.label: ‘Indication’ threshold met
issues.why: The court must decide whether the evidence met the low threshold that the disability “may be associated” with service, including via NAS discussions or other submissions.

issues.label: Sufficient competent evidence prong
issues.why: The court must assess whether the existing record lacked sufficient medical evidence to decide the nexus question, triggering an exam duty.

issues.label: Board’s reasons or bases on exam
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the Board adequately explained its conclusion that an exam was not required.

issues.label: AOJ reasons or bases adequacy
issues.why: The court must consider whether the AOJ’s failure to discuss NAS reports or duty-to-assist considerations reflects a predecisional development error relevant under AMA.

issues.label: Board review of AOJ DTA errors
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board properly identified and handled any predecisional duty-to-assist error requiring remand under AMA procedures.

issues.label: NAS Update 2010 relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether Update 2010 (available pre-2020) was part of the record or constructively possessed and whether VA had to address it.

issues.label: NAS category meaning
issues.why: The court must interpret the legal significance of NAS’s “inadequate/insufficient evidence” classification and whether VA may treat it as negative evidence.

issues.label: Biological mechanism discussion weight
issues.why: The court must decide how much probative value a hypothesized biological mechanism in NAS reports has for the § 5103A(d) ‘indication’ prong and for nexus.

issues.label: Direct service connection elements
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct legal framework for direct service connection (current disability, in-service event, nexus) is applied.

issues.label: Herbicide exposure fact finding
issues.why: The court must confirm whether in-service herbicide exposure is conceded/established and whether any factual dispute remains.

issues.label: Presumptive service connection exclusion
issues.why: The court must address the effect of squamous cell carcinoma not being listed under 38 C.F.R. § 3.309(e) and ensure the Board didn’t foreclose direct proof improperly.

issues.label: Use of other Board decisions
issues.why: The court must decide the permissible role of prior Board decisions as persuasive authority under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1303.

issues.label: Board’s treatment of prior decisions
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board provided adequate reasons for distinguishing the April 2015 and September 2015 decisions.

issues.label: Prior decisions as nexus indicators
issues.why: The court must decide whether submitting Board decisions that summarize medical opinions can constitute competent evidence or at least an ‘indication’ warranting an exam.

issues.label: Hearsay/competency of summaries
issues.why: The court must consider whether medical conclusions quoted or summarized in unrelated Board decisions are too attenuated/incompetent to trigger § 5103A(d).

issues.label: Triggering DTA via referenced literature
issues.why: The court must decide whether a claimant can trigger the exam duty by pointing to scientific literature referenced in other cases rather than submitting the literature itself.

issues.label: Board’s finding ‘general and conclusory’
issues.why: The court must review whether the Board clearly explained why the prior Board decisions’ references were insufficiently specific to indicate a nexus.

issues.label: Consideration of lay theory of infection
issues.why: The court must determine whether the Board properly addressed the claimant’s assertion that an infection led to the tonsillar carcinoma and its relevance to herbicide exposure.

issues.label: Competency of lay etiology assertions
issues.why: The court must consider whether the claimant’s statements about medical causation/infection are competent evidence and how they affect the exam duty.

issues.label: Reasons-or-bases on favorable evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board failed to discuss potentially favorable material issues raised by the record, including any NAS-related theories arguably in the record.

issues.label: Compliance with 38 U.S.C. § 7104(d)
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board’s statement of reasons or bases enables understanding and judicial review.

issues.label: Prejudicial error analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether any identified error (record scope, constructive possession, exam duty, reasons/bases) was prejudicial and could have affected the outcome.

issues.label: Appropriate remedy under AMA
issues.why: The court must decide whether the proper remedy is remand for predecisional duty-to-assist correction (exam/opinion) and/or for consideration of constructively possessed NAS reports.

issues.label: Secretary’s obligation to address NAS
issues.why: The court must decide whether VA must explicitly consider and discuss NAS updates when adjudicating herbicide-related direct service-connection claims.

issues.label: Standard of review application
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (clearly erroneous for factual findings, de novo for legal questions, arbitrary/capricious where applicable).

issues.label: Characterization of claimed condition
issues.why: The court must ensure the diagnosis (right tonsil/oropharynx SCC) is correctly characterized and not improperly analogized to excluded presumptive categories.

issues.label: Theory of entitlement identification
issues.why: The court must decide whether the Board reasonably captured all theories raised (Agent Orange nexus, infection-mediated mechanism) within the constraints of the AMA record.

issues.label: Harmlessness of dismissing 2018 decision
issues.why: The court must confirm that excluding the unrelated 2018 effective-date Board decision has no bearing on the service-connection issue and does not affect the duty-to-assist analysis.
